containers.note: List area; web crt.DataTable maps to mobile crt.List.

components.note: Folder tree. The mobile template (BaseMobileListTemplate) already provides the FolderTreeActions element; carry the web folder-schema binding (sourceSchemaName + rootSchemaName) onto it by merge-by-name so the mobile folder tree resolves the section entity. Without this the web crt.FolderTree node (inherited template chrome) is pruned and rootSchemaName is lost.

templates.note: Tabbed record page (Tabs + Feed + Attachments). Preferred target for web tabbed record pages.

containers.note: The mobile template provides the Feed and Attachments tabs (FeedTab, AttachmentsTab) — they stay LAST. Converted web tabs already arrive with explicit indexes right after the general tab (see convertedTabPlacement), so applying the element map verbatim yields: general tab, converted web tabs, Feed, Attachments.
Feed tab content; the FeedTab stays the second-to-last tab (before Attachments).
Attachments tab content; the AttachmentsTab stays the LAST tab.
All tabs except Feed and Attachments should be moved to Tabs

Web card-content wrapper; its non-tab content (side/profile) fills the mobile general tab's grid. The profile island itself is the exception — see the SideAreaProfileContainer entry: it merges into AreaProfileContainer, not into the general tab's grid.

Web profile island (the styled side-area grid with color/borderRadius). Merge twin — do NOT recreate it: the mobile template already provides AreaProfileContainer inside GeneralTabContainer as the profile card, so this wrapper's children are placed INSIDE AreaProfileContainer (never directly into GeneralTabContainer, and never leave AreaProfileContainer empty). Sibling side-area blocks (e.g. a second card like CaseInfoContainer) are NOT the island — they stay ordinary inserts into GeneralTabContainer. The island's own styling is template-provided and is not carried; if the web wrapper carries a BOUND visible or is targeted by business rules, move that logic onto AreaProfileContainer or each promoted child — it is not carried automatically.
Content ABOVE the web card-content wrapper (e.g. a progress bar) is placed above the mobile Tabs (in the Tabs' parent container).
Content BELOW the web card-content wrapper is placed below the mobile Tabs.

templates.note: Base record page (non-tabbed). Web BasePageFreedomTemplate maps to the mobile base record page.
Blank page. Mobile blank exposes only the Scaffold root.
Base page template; maps to the mobile base record page. Universal fallback container is MainContainer.
Base web template root; maps to the mobile structural root. Universal fallback container is MainContainer.

components.note: Boolean fields on mobile use crt.Toggle instead of the web crt.Checkbox.
Rich text on mobile uses crt.RichTextEditor instead of the web crt.HtmlEditor.

Web grid → mobile crt.List + crt.ListItem. The crt.ListItem must be added INTO the crt.List's `itemLayout` — it defines the row layout (`title` + `body`). Map each grid column's `code` to a `$<code>` binding: the first column becomes the ListItem `title`, the remaining columns become its `body` rows (`{ "value": "$<code>" }`); the grid `items` binding carries over to the list `items`. A column's `code` is its bound attribute name. Note: if the mobile template already provides the `List`/`ListItem` elements, configure them by merge-by-name (the row goes on the `ListItem` element) rather than inserting new ones.
Many->one: mobile FolderTreeActions is produced from web crt.FolderTree (primary); web crt.FolderTreeActions is consumed. Values are reconciled against the mobile component's registry contract.

tabAreaLayers.note: every converter-created tab gets the designer's 2-layer body — a grid 'tab body' (MainTabContainer_<suffix>) holding the tab's Area card (GridContainer_<suffix>) that receives ALL of the tab's top-level content, expansion panels included. Mirrors TabItemFactory.getMobileTabContainerConfig().

insertValueOverrides.note: Spacing normalization: mobile follows the mobile spacing standard, so the web grid's gap (typically columnGap large / rowGap none) is IGNORED, not translated — every inserted grid container (converted and synthesized alike) gets Medium row/column spacing. Keep in sync with tabAreaLayers container gaps.
Spacing normalization: the web flex gap (token, px number or CSS string) is IGNORED, not translated — every inserted flex container gets Medium gap.

Metric style normalization (ENG-94230): mobile metrics follow the mobile design standard, so the web widget's text size and border are IGNORED, not translated — every inserted indicator widget gets extra-small text with the border hidden (the 'plain white' look; the default 'without-fill' theme is left alone). The value is an OBJECT, so it MERGES into the converted config — config.data (the aggregation/providing subtree, without which the widget renders nothing) and config.title survive untouched. fontSizeMode accepts extra-small|small|medium|large|extra-large; hide-border lives at layout.border.hidden (WidgetBorderConfig), there is no top-level size/hideBorder input.

emptyContainerRemoval.note: a converter-created container of one of these types whose items receive NO surviving child is dropped deterministically (bottom-up, so emptiness cascades). A CLOSED allowlist — 'can hold children' (crt.List, crt.Tabs) is not 'safe to delete when empty'; widening it is an explicit decision here, never registry inference. crt.ExpansionPanel is judged on items only (tools content is discarded with it, called out in the drop reason). Template merge twins and synthesized tab layers are structurally out of scope.

convertedTabPlacement.note: every SURVIVING converted web tab inserted under the mobile Tabs gets an explicit index starting at firstIndex (1 = right after the template's general tab), in web tree order — so the template's FeedTab/AttachmentsTab stay LAST and the applied order is: general tab, converted web tabs, Feed, Attachments. Runs after empty-container removal (a tab removed as empty gets no index — no holes) and after positional-index compaction (which rebases each group to 0 and must never see these indexes). Absent section switches the pass off — converted tabs then append, as before.
